# Fully pinned, hash-verified dependency set for bzt in the jmeter engine image.
#
# Why this exists: 'pip3 install bzt==1.16.51' pinned bzt and nothing else.
# Its ~50 transitive dependencies floated, so two builds of the same
# Dockerfile produced different images. --require-hashes closes that, and
# makes a substituted or re-published artifact fail the build instead of
# shipping silently (Scorecard PinnedDependenciesID, pipCommand).
#
# Deliberately separate from the k6 engine's file: this resolves against
# Python 3.10 (jammy's python3), and the two do not agree -- numpy differs (2.2.6 on 3.10 vs
# 2.5.2 on 3.12) and 3.10 additionally pulls async-timeout. One shared file
# would break one of the two images.
#
# Generated with --allow-unsafe, which is required rather than optional
# here: without it pip-compile omits setuptools/wheel, and the build then
# fails on 'Hashes are required in --require-hashes mode' when a package
# needs setuptools to build from sdist. Found by building, not by reading.
#
# Regenerate after changing the bzt version, inside THAT image's own base
# (the base fixes the Python version, which fixes the resolution):
#   echo 'bzt==<version>' > req.in
#   pip-compile --generate-hashes --allow-unsafe --output-file=- req.in
#
aiodogstatsd==0.16.0.post0 \
    --hash=sha256:82000e6da599aee92e3c129d8cdf05cd102e2ac7a8a7da7ec07a16967031c865 \
    --hash=sha256:f783c7d6d74edd160b34141ff5f069c9a935bb32636823e39e36f0d1dbe14931
    # via molotov
